answer.evidence: The grade mapping is in radon/metrics.py:150-157. mi_rank returns chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0)). Score 9 gives 'C' and score 19 gives 'B', which matches the docstring (A if score > 19, B if 9 < score <= 19, C if score <= 9). Both boundaries are inclusive on the lower grade. I only read metrics.py and grepped the other files; I did not run the code. The boolean-arithmetic expression is hard to read and should have explicit boundary tests at 8.99, 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01. Non-numeric or NaN input is another case to test. Review time goes to radon/raw.py and radon/visitors.py, which provide the inputs to the maintainability index (LOC/comment counts from raw, Halstead and complexity figures from visitors). Check that these feed mi_compute correctly, because wrong inputs would shift scores across the 9 and 19 thresholds. radon/metrics.py gets a shorter pass for the rank function itself. radon/complexity.py gets a brief check that cc_rank is a separate scheme and does not share these thresholds.
